name: Lebu Wolof
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Ndiaye, Ousmane. 2013. Contrastive study of Saalum-Saalum Wolof and Lebu: phonology and morphology (55 pp.); Diop, Abdou Kounta. 2001. Dialectologie Wolof: le Lébou de Ouakam
earlier_scan.note: Two Lebu phonology-covering dialect studies exist; neither found online

sources.citation: Robert, Stéphane. 2011. Le wolof. In E. Bonvini, J. Busuttil & A. Peyraube (eds), Dictionnaire des langues, 23-30. Paris: PUF (HAL halshs-00642854).
sources.note: Wolof-general; on Lebu only says 'le parler lébou, utilisé dans la presqu'île du Cap-Vert et avec lequel l'inter-compréhension est difficile' — no Lebu-specific prosody.

sources.citation: Voisin, Sylvie. 2023. Le wolof et ses variétés. La Linguistique 59(2): 69-99. doi:10.3917/ling.592.0069 (HAL hal-04278103, author version, 19 pp.)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Section 2.3.1 'Lebu' is historical/sociolinguistic; the article's data are morphosyntactic (noun classes, possession, conjugation). Useful as the survey of record: lists the Lebu descriptions (Diop 1994, 2001; Dramé 2012; Diagne 2015; Diouf 2016; Voisin & Dramé 2019; Voisin 2021) and notes Lebu is the most divergent Wolof variety, sometimes treated as a separate language.

sources.citation: Voisin, Sylvie & Mamour Dramé. 2019. L'inaccompli dans différentes variétés de wolof. Africana Linguistica 25: 321-386 (HAL hal-03943672).
sources.note: Nothing; TAM morphology across Wolof varieties incl. Lebu of Ouakam and Yéne (authors' own fieldwork). States (p. 330) that Dramé 2012 'propose une comparaison de la phonologie et d'une partie de la morphologie de trois variétés, le wolof du Saloum, le lébou de Ouakam et le wolof commun' and that Diop 2001 described the Lebu of Ouakam.

sources.citation: Diouf, Jean Léopold. 2016 [PDF created 2015]. Particularités du lébu : un dialecte wolof. Manuscrit, projet ANR Sénélangues (ANR-09-BLAN-0326). 359 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Contents = introduction, morphosyntactic particularities (demonstratives, possessives, pronouns, koon irrealis, incitative/negation), short lexicon, ~310 pp of interlinearised Petite-Côte Lebu texts (Yéen, Ndittax, Ngapparu, Géeréw, Rufisque, Kel/Tubaab-Jalaaw). No phonology chapter; no mention of accent, tone, prosody or intonation.

sources.citation: Diagne, Mbacké & Jean Léopold Diouf. n.d. Wolof lébou. Fiche langue, projet Sénélangues (1 p.).
sources.note: Nothing; location, speaker numbers (~90,000), endangered, survey sites (Rufisque, Ouakam, Bargny, Yenne, Toubab Jalaw).

sources.citation: Robert, Stéphane. 2024. Wolof: a grammatical sketch; and Lüpke, F. (ed.) The Oxford Guide to the Atlantic Languages of West Africa. Oxford: OUP.
